subject: maths
title: Coordinates in Four Quadrants, Translations and Reflections
seo_title: Year 6 Coordinates Worksheets: Four Quadrants, Translations and Reflections
standard_text: Describe positions on the full coordinate grid (all four quadrants); draw and translate simple shapes on the coordinate plane, and reflect them in the axes.
meta_desc: Free Year 6 maths worksheets on coordinates in all four quadrants: plot points with negative coordinates, translate and reflect shapes in the axes, find missing vertices and solve SATs-style problems. 100 questions with an answer key, following the National Curriculum.
key_big: (x, y): x says left or right, y says up or down, and a minus sign means left or down.
key_sub: A translation changes x for left/right moves and y for up/down moves. Reflecting in the x-axis changes the sign of y; reflecting in the y-axis changes the sign of x. Across an axis, add the distances on each side.
body_html:
The four quadrants

In Year 6 the x-axis and the y-axis carry on past 0 into negative numbers. They cross at the origin, (0, 0), and split the grid into four quadrants.

Coordinates (x, y) still go along the corridor, then up (or down) the stairs. The sign tells the direction. Positive x: right. Negative x: left. Positive y: up. Negative y: down.

WhereSigns (x, y)Example
top right(+, +)(2, 5)
top left(−, +)(−3, 4)
bottom left(−, −)(−6, −1)
bottom right(+, −)(4, −2)

A point on an axis has a 0 in it, like (0, −4) or (5, 0).

Translations

A translation slides a point or shape without turning it. Left and right change only x. Up and down change only y. When you cross an axis, count to 0, then keep going.

Example

Describe the translation from (−3, 2) to (4, −1).

Across: −3 to 4 is 3 squares to the y-axis, then 4 more: 7 right. Up and down: 2 to −1 is 3 down.

Answer: 7 squares right and 3 squares down

Reflections in the axes

An axis works like a mirror. Reflecting in the x-axis changes the sign of y. Reflecting in the y-axis changes the sign of x. Each vertex stays the same distance from the mirror line.

Example

Reflect (−4, 5) in the x-axis.

The x-axis is the mirror, so the point flips down. x stays −4. y changes sign: 5 → −5.

Answer: (−4, −5)

Missing vertices and side lengths

The missing vertex of a rectangle shares its x-coordinate with one vertex and its y-coordinate with another. For a side that crosses an axis, add the distances on each side: from −4 to 2 is 4 + 2 = 6.

Example

A parallelogram ABCD has A (−3, −2), B (2, −2) and C (4, 1). Find D.

From B to C is 2 right and 3 up. Do the same move from A: (−3 + 2, −2 + 3).

Answer: (−1, 1)

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Swapping the numbers: plotting (−3, 4) at (4, −3)Across first (x), then up or down (y)
Sign errors at an axis: 2 − 4 = 2Count to 0, then keep going: 2 − 4 = −2
Finding −4 to 3 as 4 − 3 = 1Opposite sides of an axis: add, 4 + 3 = 7
Reflecting in the wrong axisIn the x-axis, y changes sign. In the y-axis, x changes sign
Changing only one coordinate in “4 left and 3 down”Change x for left/right and y for up/down

faq.q: What do children learn about coordinates in Year 6?
faq.a: Year 6 pupils use the full coordinate grid in all four quadrants. They plot points with negative coordinates, translate shapes and reflect them in the x-axis and y-axis.

faq.q: How do you reflect a shape in the x-axis?
faq.a: Reflect each vertex: keep the x-coordinate and change the sign of the y-coordinate, so (3, 2) becomes (3, −2). Then join the new vertices.

faq.q: How do you describe a translation on a coordinate grid?
faq.a: Follow one vertex and say how many squares it moves left or right and up or down, for example “6 squares right and 5 squares down”. Every vertex moves the same way.

faq.q: Are coordinates in the Year 6 SATs?
faq.a: Yes. The KS2 reasoning papers can include questions on coordinates in all four quadrants, translations, reflections and finding missing vertices of shapes.

sets.title: Read and plot points in all four quadrants

items.q: What are the coordinates of point A?
items.e: Start at the origin, go 2 left, then 5 up. Point A is at (−2, 5). The x-coordinate comes first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point B?
items.e: Start at the origin, go 4 right, then 3 down. Point B is at (4, −3). The x-coordinate comes first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point C?
items.e: Start at the origin, go 5 left, then 2 down. Point C is at (−5, −2). The x-coordinate comes first; a minus sign means left or down. (−2, −5) is point D: the numbers are swapped.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point E?
items.e: Start at the origin, go 3 right, then 6 down. Point E is at (3, −6). The x-coordinate comes first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point F?
items.e: Start at the origin, go 4 left, then 1 up. Point F is at (−4, 1). The x-coordinate comes first; a minus sign means left or down. (1, −4) is point G: the numbers are swapped.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point H?
items.e: Start at the origin, go 6 left, then 3 down. Point H is at (−6, −3). The x-coordinate comes first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point J?
items.e: Start at the origin, go 0 left or right, then 5 down. Point J is at (0, −5). The x-coordinate comes first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point M?
items.e: Start at the origin, go 3 left, then 0 up or down. Point M is at (−3, 0). The x-coordinate comes first; a minus sign means left or down.

items.q: What is the x-coordinate of point P?
items.e: Point P is 5 squares to the left of the y-axis, so x = −5. Left means negative. (3 is its y-coordinate.)

items.q: What is the y-coordinate of point Q?
items.e: Point Q is 4 squares below the x-axis, so y = −4. Down means negative. (2 is its x-coordinate.)

items.q: Which point is at (−4, 3)?
items.e: Start at the origin, go 4 left, then 3 up: that is point D. Point A is at (3, −4): the numbers are swapped. Point B is at (4, 3): the sign of x is wrong.

items.q: Which point is at (3, −5)?
items.e: Start at the origin, go 3 right, then 5 down: that is point B. Point A is at (−5, 3): the numbers are swapped. Point C is at (−3, −5): the sign of x is wrong.

items.q: Which point is at (−2, −5)?
items.e: Start at the origin, go 2 left, then 5 down: that is point C. Point A is at (−5, −2): the numbers are swapped. Point B is at (2, −5): the sign of x is wrong.

items.q: Which point is at (−5, 1)?
items.e: Start at the origin, go 5 left, then 1 up: that is point A. Point B is at (1, −5): the numbers are swapped. Point C is at (5, 1): the sign of x is wrong.

items.q: Which point is at (0, 4)?
items.e: Start at the origin, go 0 left or right, then 4 up: that is point D. Point A is at (4, 0): the numbers are swapped.

items.q: To plot (−3, 5), what do you do first from the origin?
items.e: The first number, −3, is the x-coordinate. It is negative, so go 3 left. Then go 5 up.

items.q: What does a negative x-coordinate tell you?
c: The point is right of the y-axis
The point is left of the y-axis
The point is below the x-axis
The point is above the x-axis
items.e: The x-coordinate says how far left or right to go. Positive means right; negative means left of the y-axis.

items.q: Ava starts at the origin. She goes 5 left, then 2 down. What are the coordinates of her point?
items.e: 5 left gives x = −5. 2 down gives y = −2. Write x first: (−5, −2).

items.q: A point is 4 squares to the left of the y-axis and 6 squares above the x-axis. What are its coordinates?
items.e: Left of the y-axis means x is negative: x = −4. Above the x-axis means y is positive: y = 6. The point is (−4, 6).

items.q: Which point is below the x-axis and to the left of the y-axis?
items.e: Left of the y-axis: x is negative. Below the x-axis: y is negative. Only (−3, −1) has both coordinates negative. ((0, −3) is on the y-axis, not to the left of it.)

items.q: Point A is at (2, 1). It is translated 4 squares left and 3 squares down. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Left 4 changes x: 2 − 4 = −2. Down 3 changes y: 1 − 3 = −2. The new point is (−2, −2). When you cross an axis, count to 0 first, then keep going.

items.q: Point A is at (−3, 4). It is translated 5 squares right and 2 squares down. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Right 5 changes x: −3 + 5 = 2. Down 2 changes y: 4 − 2 = 2. The new point is (2, 2). When you cross an axis, count to 0 first, then keep going.

items.q: Point A is at (−1, −2). It is translated 6 squares up. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: x stays −1. Up 6 changes y: −2 + 6 = 4. The new point is (−1, 4). When you cross an axis, count to 0 first, then keep going.

items.q: Point A is at (4, −3). It is translated 6 squares left. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Left 6 changes x: 4 − 6 = −2. y stays −3. The new point is (−2, −3). When you cross an axis, count to 0 first, then keep going.

items.q: Point A is at (3, 5). It is translated 7 squares left and 4 squares down. What are its new coordinates?
items.e: Left 7 changes x: 3 − 7 = −4. Down 4 changes y: 5 − 4 = 1. The new point is (−4, 1). When you cross an axis, count to 0 first, then keep going.

items.q: Point P is translated 5 squares left and 4 squares down. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: Left 5 changes x: 3 − 5 = −2. Down 4 changes y: 2 − 4 = −2. The new point is (−2, −2). When you cross an axis, count to 0 first, then keep going. That is point D.

items.q: Point P is translated 6 squares right and 3 squares up. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: Right 6 changes x: −4 + 6 = 2. Up 3 changes y: −1 + 3 = 2. The new point is (2, 2). When you cross an axis, count to 0 first, then keep going. That is point C.

items.q: Point P is translated 3 squares left and 7 squares up. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: Left 3 changes x: 1 − 3 = −2. Up 7 changes y: −4 + 7 = 3. The new point is (−2, 3). When you cross an axis, count to 0 first, then keep going. That is point B.

items.q: Point P is translated 4 squares right and 8 squares down. Which point shows where it lands?
items.e: Right 4 changes x: −2 + 4 = 2. Down 8 changes y: 5 − 8 = −3. The new point is (2, −3). When you cross an axis, count to 0 first, then keep going. That is point A.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (−3, 2) and B is at (4, −1). Across: −3 to 4 is 7 squares right (3 to the axis, then 4 more). Up and down: 2 to −1 is 3 squares down (2 to the axis, then 1 more).

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (2, 4) and B is at (−3, 1). Across: 2 to −3 is 5 squares left (2 to the axis, then 3 more). Up and down: 4 to 1 is 3 squares down.

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (−4, −3) and B is at (1, 2). Across: −4 to 1 is 5 squares right (4 to the axis, then 1 more). Up and down: −3 to 2 is 5 squares up (3 to the axis, then 2 more).

items.q: Point A is translated to point B. Describe the translation.
items.e: A is at (5, −1) and B is at (−2, −1). Across: 5 to −2 is 7 squares left (5 to the axis, then 2 more). y stays −1, so there is no move up or down.

items.q: A shape’s vertex moves from (−5, 4) to (1, −2). Describe the translation.
items.e: The start is at (−5, 4) and the end is at (1, −2). Across: −5 to 1 is 6 squares right (5 to the axis, then 1 more). Up and down: 4 to −2 is 6 squares down (4 to the axis, then 2 more).

items.q: A shape’s vertex moves from (3, −5) to (−1, 2). Describe the translation.
items.e: The start is at (3, −5) and the end is at (−1, 2). Across: 3 to −1 is 4 squares left (3 to the axis, then 1 more). Up and down: −5 to 2 is 7 squares up (5 to the axis, then 2 more).

items.q: Point B is translated 4 squares left and 3 squares up. It lands on (−1, 2). Where did it start?
items.e: Work backwards and undo each move. 4 left is undone by 4 right: −1 + 4 = 3. 3 up is undone by 3 down: 2 − 3 = −1. B started at (3, −1).

items.q: Lily translates (3, −1) 4 squares left and gets (1, −1). What mistake did she make?
items.e: Left 4 from x = 3: 3 − 4 = −1. It goes 3 squares to the y-axis, then 1 more. The answer is (−1, −1), not (1, −1).

items.q: A triangle has vertices at (−4, 1), (−1, 1) and (−4, 5). It is translated 5 squares right and 6 squares down. What are the new coordinates of the vertex at (−1, 1)?
items.e: Right 5 changes x: −1 + 5 = 4. Down 6 changes y: 1 − 6 = −5. The new point is (4, −5). When you cross an axis, count to 0 first, then keep going. Every vertex moves in the same way, so the shape stays the same size.

items.q: Shape A is translated to shape B. Describe the translation.
items.e: Follow one vertex. The bottom-left vertex of A is at (−5, 1) and of B is at (1, −4). Across: −5 to 1 is 6 squares right (5 to the axis, then 1 more). Down: 1 to −4 is 5 squares down (1 to the axis, then 4 more). That is 6 squares right and 5 squares down. Every vertex moves the same way.

items.q: A square has vertices at (1, 1), (4, 1), (4, 4) and (1, 4). It is translated 6 squares left and 5 squares down. Which list shows the new vertices?
items.e: Subtract 6 from every x-coordinate and 5 from every y-coordinate. For example, (1, 1) → (1 − 6 = −5, 1 − 5 = −4) = (−5, −4).

sets.title: Reflections in the x-axis and y-axis

items.q: Reflect (3, −2) in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: In the y-axis, the point flips left or right: y stays −2 and x changes sign, 3 → −3. The image is (−3, −2).

items.q: Reflect (−4, 5) in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: In the x-axis, the point flips up or down: x stays −4 and y changes sign, 5 → −5. The image is (−4, −5).

items.q: Reflect (5, 1) in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: In the y-axis, the point flips left or right: y stays 1 and x changes sign, 5 → −5. The image is (−5, 1).

items.q: Reflect (−2, −6) in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: In the x-axis, the point flips up or down: x stays −2 and y changes sign, −6 → 6. The image is (−2, 6).

items.q: Reflect (−6, −3) in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: In the y-axis, the point flips left or right: y stays −3 and x changes sign, −6 → 6. The image is (6, −3).

items.q: Reflect (0, 5) in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: (0, 5) is on the y-axis, the mirror line itself, so it does not move: (0, 5).

items.q: Reflect (−4, 0) in the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the image?
items.e: (−4, 0) is on the x-axis, the mirror line itself, so it does not move: (−4, 0).

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the x-axis?
items.e: P is at (−3, 2). In the x-axis, the point flips up or down: x stays −3 and y changes sign, 2 → −2. The image is (−3, −2). That is point D. Point A is the reflection in the y-axis instead.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the y-axis?
items.e: P is at (4, −2). In the y-axis, the point flips left or right: y stays −2 and x changes sign, 4 → −4. The image is (−4, −2). That is point B. Point A is the reflection in the x-axis instead.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the x-axis?
items.e: P is at (−2, −5). In the x-axis, the point flips up or down: x stays −2 and y changes sign, −5 → 5. The image is (−2, 5). That is point A. Point B is the reflection in the y-axis instead.

items.q: Which point is the reflection of point P in the y-axis?
items.e: P is at (5, 3). In the y-axis, the point flips left or right: y stays 3 and x changes sign, 5 → −5. The image is (−5, 3). That is point C. Point A is the reflection in the x-axis instead.

items.q: The points (−5, 2) and (5, 2) are reflections of each other in which axis?
items.e: Only the x-coordinate changes sign (−5 → 5), so the points flip left and right. The mirror line is the y-axis.

items.q: The points (3, −4) and (3, 4) are reflections of each other in which axis?
items.e: Only the y-coordinate changes sign (−4 → 4), so the points flip up and down. The mirror line is the x-axis.

items.q: How has shape A moved to shape B?
items.e: Each vertex keeps its x-coordinate and its y-coordinate changes sign, for example (5, 1) → (5, −1). Shape B is a mirror image below the x-axis.

items.q: How has shape A moved to shape B?
items.e: Each vertex keeps its y-coordinate and its x-coordinate changes sign, for example (−5, 1) → (5, 1). The right angle is now on the right: a mirror image in the y-axis.

items.q: How has shape A moved to shape B?
items.e: Every vertex moved 6 squares left and 6 squares down, for example (1, 2) → (−5, −4). The shape faces the same way, so it slid: a translation, not a reflection.

items.q: A triangle has vertices at (−4, 1), (−1, 1) and (−4, 5). It is reflected in the x-axis. Which list shows the vertices of the image?
items.e: In the x-axis, keep each x and change the sign of each y: (−4, 1) → (−4, −1), (−1, 1) → (−1, −1), (−4, 5) → (−4, −5). Change every vertex, not just some.

items.q: When you reflect a point in the y-axis, what changes?
items.e: The y-axis is a mirror standing up and down. The point flips left or right, so only x changes sign. Example: (4, 3) → (−4, 3).

items.q: A rectangle has vertices at (1, −2), (5, −2), (5, −4) and (1, −4). It is reflected in the y-axis. What are the coordinates of the image of (5, −2)?
items.e: In the y-axis, the point flips left or right: y stays −2 and x changes sign, 5 → −5. The image is (−5, −2). The image rectangle is to the left of the y-axis, the same distance away.

items.q: Arjun reflects (2, 5) in the x-axis and gets (−2, 5). What mistake did he make?
items.e: Arjun changed the sign of x, which is a reflection in the y-axis. In the x-axis, y changes sign: (2, −5).

sets.title: Missing vertices and side lengths across the axes

items.q: A, B and C are 3 vertices of a rectangle. What are the coordinates of the 4th vertex, D?
items.e: D is in line with A up and down, so x = −4. It is in line with C across, so y = −2. D is at (−4, −2).

items.q: A, B and C are 3 vertices of a rectangle. What are the coordinates of the 4th vertex, D?
items.e: D is in line with C up and down, so x = 3. It is in line with A across, so y = −4. D is at (3, −4).

items.q: A, B and C are 3 vertices of a square. What are the coordinates of the 4th vertex, D?
items.e: D is in line with A up and down, so x = 2. It is in line with C across, so y = −3. D is at (2, −3).

items.q: A, B and C are 3 vertices of parallelogram ABCD. What are the coordinates of D?
items.e: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are parallel and equal. To go from B to A you move 5 squares left. Make the same move from C: (3, 2) → (−2, 2). D is at (−2, 2).

items.q: A, B and C are 3 vertices of parallelogram ABCD. What are the coordinates of D?
items.e: Opposite sides of a parallelogram are parallel and equal. To go from B to A you move 2 squares left and 4 squares up. Make the same move from C: (3, −1) → (1, 3). D is at (1, 3).

items.q: The red dots are 3 vertices of a square. Which point is the 4th vertex?
items.e: The missing vertex lines up with the red ones: x = −3 (above (−3, −2)) and y = 2 (across from (1, 2)). That is (−3, 2), point B.

items.q: A rectangle has vertices at (−2, 5), (4, 5) and (4, −3). What are the coordinates of the 4th vertex?
items.e: The vertices of a rectangle use just two x-coordinates (−2 and 4) and two y-coordinates (−3 and 5). The pair not used yet is (−2, −3).

items.q: A square has vertices at (−1, −1), (3, −1) and (3, 3). What are the coordinates of the 4th vertex?
items.e: The vertices of a square use just two x-coordinates (−1 and 3) and two y-coordinates (−1 and 3). The pair not used yet is (−1, 3).

items.q: A rectangle has vertices at (−5, −2), (3, 4) and (−5, 4). What are the coordinates of the 4th vertex?
items.e: The vertices of a rectangle use just two x-coordinates (−5 and 3) and two y-coordinates (−2 and 4). The pair not used yet is (3, −2).

items.q: ABCD is a parallelogram. A is at (−3, −2), B is at (2, −2) and C is at (4, 1). What are the coordinates of D?
items.e: From B to C you move 2 right and 3 up. The opposite side AD makes the same move: (−3, −2) → (−1, 1). ((−3, 1) would make a rectangle, not this parallelogram.)

items.q: How long is the side AB? Give your answer in squares.
items.e: Both points have x = 2. They are on opposite sides of the x-axis: 4 to the axis, then 3 more. 4 + 3 = 7. Add the two parts; do not subtract them or use just one.

items.q: How long is the side CD? Give your answer in squares.
items.e: Both points have y = 1. They are on opposite sides of the y-axis: 5 to the axis, then 3 more. 5 + 3 = 8. Add the two parts; do not subtract them or use just one.

items.q: How long is the side EF? Give your answer in squares.
items.e: Both points have x = −3. They are on opposite sides of the x-axis: 2 to the axis, then 4 more. 2 + 4 = 6. Add the two parts; do not subtract them or use just one.

items.q: A side of a shape goes from (−6, −4) to (−1, −4). How long is it?
items.e: Both points have y = −4. They are on the same side of the y-axis: 6 − 1 = 5.

items.q: A side of a shape goes from (0, −5) to (0, 4). How long is it?
items.e: Both points have x = 0. They are on opposite sides of the x-axis: 5 to the axis, then 4 more. 5 + 4 = 9.

items.q: A side of a shape goes from (−4, 3) to (−4, −2). How long is it?
items.e: Both points have x = −4. They are on opposite sides of the x-axis: 3 to the axis, then 2 more. 3 + 2 = 5.

items.q: A rectangle has vertices at (−3, 2), (4, 2), (4, −1) and (−3, −1). What is its perimeter?
items.e: Length: −3 to 4 is 3 + 4 = 7 squares. Width: −1 to 2 is 1 + 2 = 3 squares. Perimeter = 7 + 3 + 7 + 3 = 20 squares. (Doing 4 − 3 and 2 − 1 gives sides of 1 and a perimeter of 4.)

items.q: A square has vertices at (−3, −3), (3, −3), (3, 3) and (−3, 3). What is its perimeter?
items.e: Each side goes from −3 to 3: 3 + 3 = 6 squares. Perimeter = 4 × 6 = 24 squares. (3 − 3 = 0 comes from subtracting instead of adding; 28 comes from counting 7 dots on each side.)

items.q: A rectangle has vertices at (−5, 3), (2, 3), (2, −2) and (−5, −2). Each square is 1 cm². What is its area?
items.e: Length: 5 + 2 = 7 cm (opposite sides of the y-axis). Width: 3 + 2 = 5 cm (opposite sides of the x-axis). Area = 7 × 5 = 35 cm².

items.q: A square has vertices at (−2, −1) and (3, −1). The other two vertices are above the x-axis. What are the coordinates of the vertex straight above (3, −1)?
items.e: The side from (−2, −1) to (3, −1) is 2 + 3 = 5 squares long. All sides of a square are equal, so go 5 up from (3, −1): −1 + 5 = 4. The vertex is at (3, 4).

items.q: Point (2, 3) is translated 5 squares left and 1 square down. Then it is reflected in the x-axis. Where does it end up?
items.e: Do the moves in order. Translate: (2, 3) → (−3, 2). Reflect in the x-axis (y changes sign): (−3, 2) → (−3, −2). Reflecting first gives a different answer, (−3, −4).

items.q: Point (−4, −1) is reflected in the y-axis. Then it is translated 2 squares left and 5 squares up. Where does it end up?
items.e: Reflect in the y-axis (x changes sign): (−4, −1) → (4, −1). Translate: x: 4 − 2 = 2. y: −1 + 5 = 4. It ends at (2, 4).

items.q: Triangle PQR is translated 6 squares left. Then it is reflected in the x-axis. What are the new coordinates of Q?
items.e: Q is at (4, 1). 6 left: 4 − 6 = −2, so Q moves to (−2, 1). Reflect in the x-axis: (−2, 1) → (−2, −1).

items.q: A translation moves point A from (−3, 2) to (2, −1). The same translation moves point B from (1, 4). Where does B go?
items.e: A moves 5 right (−3 to 2) and 3 down (2 to −1). Move B the same way: (1, 4) → (6, 1).

items.q: ABCD is a rectangle. A is at (−5, 2) and C is at (3, −4). B is straight to the right of A. What are the coordinates of D?
items.e: B is right of A, so B = (3, 2). D is opposite B: straight below A and straight across from C. D takes x from A and y from C: (−5, −4).

items.q: A square has its centre at the origin. Its sides are parallel to the axes. One vertex is at (3, 3). What are the coordinates of the vertex below the x-axis and to the left of the y-axis?
items.e: The square is symmetrical about both axes, so its vertices are (3, 3), (−3, 3), (−3, −3) and (3, −3). Left and below means both are negative: (−3, −3).

items.q: The points (−6, 5), (−4, 3), (−2, 1) and (0, −1) follow a pattern. What is the next point?
items.e: Each time x goes up by 2 and y goes down by 2. Next: x = 0 + 2 = 2 and y = −1 − 2 = −3.

items.q: The points (−5, −4), (−3, −1) and (−1, 2) lie on a straight line. The steps stay the same. What is the next point?
items.e: Each step is 2 right and 3 up: −5 + 2 = −3 and −4 + 3 = −1. Next: −1 + 2 = 1 and 2 + 3 = 5.

items.q: In the points (−2, −4), (−1, −3), (0, −2) and (1, −1), the y-coordinate is always 2 less than the x-coordinate. Which point also fits the rule?
items.e: Check y = x − 2. For (5, 3): 5 − 2 = 3. Yes. For (3, 5): 3 − 2 = 1, not 5 (the numbers are swapped). For (−5, −3): −5 − 2 = −7, not −3.

items.q: Point P is at (a, 3). It is reflected in the y-axis and lands on (−4, 3). What is the value of a?
items.e: A reflection in the y-axis changes the sign of x. The image has x = −4, so P has x = 4. a = 4.

items.q: Point Q is at (−2, b). It is reflected in the x-axis and lands on (−2, 5). What is the value of b?
items.e: A reflection in the x-axis changes the sign of y. The image has y = 5, so Q has y = −5. b = −5.

items.q: The map shows the school field. The origin is the centre circle. T = tree, B = bench, P = pond, S = shed. Each square is 10 m. What are the coordinates of the shed?
items.e: Start at the origin, go 5 right, then 2 down. The shed is at (5, −2).

items.q: The map shows the school field. The origin is the centre circle. T = tree, B = bench, P = pond, S = shed. Each square is 10 m. Ethan starts at the tree. He walks 7 squares right and 1 square up. Where is he now?
items.e: The tree is at (−4, 3). 7 right: −4 + 7 = 3. 1 up: 3 + 1 = 4. (3, 4) is the bench.

items.q: The map shows the school field. The origin is the centre circle. T = tree, B = bench, P = pond, S = shed. Each square is 10 m. A flag is placed at the reflection of the pond in the x-axis. What are its coordinates?
items.e: The pond is at (−3, −4). In the x-axis, x stays −3 and y changes sign: the flag is at (−3, 4).

items.q: The map shows the school field. The origin is the centre circle. T = tree, B = bench, P = pond, S = shed. Each square is 10 m. Describe the translation from the pond to the shed.
items.e: The pond is at (−3, −4) and the shed is at (5, −2). Across: −3 to 5 is 8 squares right (3 to the axis, then 5 more). Up and down: −4 to −2 is 2 squares up.

items.q: The map shows the school field. The origin is the centre circle. T = tree, B = bench, P = pond, S = shed. Each square is 10 m. A pupil walks along the grid lines from the pond to the tree by the shortest route. How many metres is that?
items.e: The pond is at (−3, −4) and the tree is at (−4, 3). Across: 1 square. Up: −4 to 3 is 4 + 3 = 7 squares. 1 + 7 = 8 squares, and 8 × 10 = 80 m.

items.q: A triangle has vertices at (1, 2), (3, 2) and (1, 5). It is reflected in the y-axis, then translated 4 squares down. Which list shows the new vertices?
items.e: Reflect in the y-axis (x changes sign): (−1, 2), (−3, 2) and (−1, 5). Then 4 down (subtract 4 from each y): (−1, −2), (−3, −2) and (−1, 1).

items.q: In a computer game, Aisha’s character starts at (−2, −3). It moves 5 squares right, 4 squares up, then 6 squares left. Where does it stop?
Two vertices of a square are at (−2, 1) and (2, 1). The rest of the square is below this side. What are the other two vertices?
items.e: The side is 2 + 2 = 4 squares long. Go 4 down from each vertex: 1 − 4 = −3.

items.q: Point M is at (−5, 4). It is reflected in the y-axis, then in the x-axis. Where does it end up?
items.e: In the y-axis: (−5, 4) → (5, 4). Then in the x-axis: (5, 4) → (5, −4). Two reflections change both signs.
